vi.B: Hãy viết cho thiên sứ của Hội Thánh tại Ê-phê-sô: "Đây là lời của Đấng nắm chặt bảy ngôi sao trong tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, Đấng đi lại giữa bảy chân đèn bằng vàng:
vi.R: Hãy viết thư này cho thiên sứ của Hội Thánh tại Ê-phê-sô: "Sứ điệp này đến từ Đấng nắm chặt bảy ngôi sao trong tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đi lại giữa bảy chân đèn bằng vàng.

ko.B: 에베소 교회의 천사에게 이렇게 써라. "오른손에 일곱 별을 꼭 쥐고 계시고, 일곱 금 등잔대 사이를 거니시는 분이 이렇게 말씀하신다.
ko.R: 에베소에 있는 교회의 천사에게 이 편지를 써라. "이것은 오른손에 일곱 별을 꼭 쥐고 계시고, 일곱 금 등잔대 사이를 거니시는 분이 보내시는 말씀이다.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: holds firmly, and walks among: his grip on the churches and his presence with them
decisions.reason: In 1:16 he "has" the stars; here κρατῶν means to grasp or hold firmly. And he does not only stand among the lampstands (1:13) but περιπατῶν, walks among them: he is present with the churches and watches over them.

decisions.choice: Ephesus: the leading city of the province of Asia
decisions.reason: Ephesus was a port and the largest city of the province, with the great temple of Artemis (Acts 19). Paul worked there for more than two years (Acts 19:10), and it is the first city a messenger from Patmos would reach.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

decisions.choice: "Voici ce que dit" (L); "Voici le message de" (B); "Ce message vient de" (R) (for all seven messages)
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word (m1). Literal keeps the verb "dit"; Balanced and Readable follow the English "This is the message of" and "This message is from". The same wording opens each of the seven messages.

decisions.choice: Esto dice (L); Este es el mensaje de (B); Este mensaje es de (R)
decisions.reason: The prophets' formula for bringing the Lord's word opens each of the seven letters. Literal keeps its short form with "esto"; Balanced and Readable say what it is, a message from the speaker, as the English does. The same wording is used at the head of every letter.

decisions.choice: the church and its angel addressed as "tú" in every letter
decisions.reason: Each letter speaks to the angel of one church in the singular, and Spanish follows with "tú" and its forms ("conozco tus obras"). Plural forms, with the plural_you span, appear only where the Greek turns to the members in the plural (2:10, 2:13, 2:23-25).

decisions.choice: Haya ndiyo anayoyasema (L); Huu ndio ujumbe wa (B); Ujumbe huu unatoka kwa (R)
decisions.reason: The prophet's formula for bringing the Lord's word (m1), in present-day Swahili rather than the old "anenayo". The same wording opens all seven letters.

decisions.choice: the opening of each of the seven letters: "Hãy viết cho thiên sứ của Hội Thánh tại ...", then "Đấng ... nói những điều này:" (L), "Đây là lời của Đấng ...:" (B), "Sứ điệp này đến từ Đấng ..." (R)
decisions.reason: "These things says" is the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word (m1), and the same words open every letter, so Vietnamese keeps one fixed form at each level through 2:1-3:14. The speaker is the risen Jesus, and the founder settled "nói" for Jesus speaking at every level; Balanced and Readable say "message", as the English does.

decisions.choice: the risen Christ speaks of himself in the opening as "Đấng ... Ngài" and then as "Ta"; he speaks to the church as "con" (singular) and "các con" (plural) in every letter
decisions.reason: Each letter is addressed to one angel, standing for one church, so most of the "you" is singular; where the Greek turns to the members (2:10, 2:13, 2:23-24), it is plural. The style guide gives Jesus "các con" for his disciples, and these are his own churches, loved even when rebuked (3:19), so Vietnamese says "con" and "các con". "Ngươi" is the solemn word of God's Old Testament speech and would make the letters sound like sentences passed on strangers. A reviewer should weigh this choice.

decisions.choice: the opening of each of the seven letters: "...에 있는 교회의 천사에게 써라" (L), "... 교회의 천사에게 이렇게 써라" (B), "...에 있는 교회의 천사에게 이 편지를 써라" (R); "...분이 이것들을 말씀하신다" (L), "...분이 이렇게 말씀하신다" (B), "이것은 ...분이 보내시는 말씀이다" (R)
decisions.reason: "These things says" is the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word (meaning decision), so each level keeps one wording for it in all seven letters (2:1, 8, 12, 18; 3:1, 7, 14), and Christ, who speaks of himself through the formula, takes the honorific in it. "천사" for the angel, as the English keeps "angel" at every level.

decisions.choice: Christ speaks to the angel of each church as "너" in 해라체, and to its members as "너희"
decisions.reason: Christ speaks in the Korean Gospels' style for Jesus (Korean style guide, Settled); each letter is addressed to one angel, standing for one church, in the singular, as in the Greek.

source.text: Οἶδα τὰ ἔργα σου, καὶ τὸν κόπον καὶ τὴν ὑπομονήν σου, καὶ ὅτι οὐ δύνῃ βαστάσαι κακούς, καὶ ἐπείρασας τοὺς λέγοντας ἑαυτοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ οὐκ εἰσίν, καὶ εὗρες αὐτοὺς ψευδεῖς·

records.literal_gloss: I know the works of you and the labor and the endurance of you, and that not you are able to bear bad [ones], and you tested those calling themselves apostles and not they are, and you found them false;

en.L: I know your works, and your labor and endurance, and that you cannot bear evil [people], and you tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and you found them false.
en.B: I know your works, how hard you have labored and how you have endured. I know that you cannot put up with people who do evil. Those who call themselves apostles, though they are not, you put to the test and found to be false.
en.R: I know everything you do. I know how hard you work and how you keep going. I know that you will not put up with evil people. Some people said they were apostles, but they were not. You tested them and found out that they were lying.

fr.L: Je connais tes œuvres, et ton labeur et ta persévérance, et [je sais] que tu ne peux pas supporter les méchants, et tu as mis à l’épreuve ceux qui se disent apôtres et ne le sont pas, et tu les as trouvés menteurs.
fr.B: Je connais tes œuvres, la peine que tu t’es donnée et ta persévérance. Je sais que tu ne peux pas supporter ceux qui font le mal. Ceux qui se disent apôtres et qui ne le sont pas, tu les as mis à l’épreuve et tu as découvert qu’ils étaient des menteurs.
fr.R: Je sais tout ce que tu fais. Je sais combien tu travailles dur et comment tu tiens bon. Je sais que tu ne supportes pas les gens mauvais. Certains disaient qu’ils étaient apôtres, mais ce n’était pas vrai. Tu les as mis à l’épreuve et tu as découvert qu’ils mentaient.

es.L: Conozco tus obras, y tu trabajo y tu perseverancia, y que no puedes soportar a [los] malos, y que pusiste a prueba a los que se llaman a sí mismos apóstoles, y no lo son, y los hallaste mentirosos.
es.B: Conozco tus obras, lo mucho que has trabajado y cómo has perseverado. Sé que no puedes tolerar a los que hacen el mal. A los que se dicen apóstoles sin serlo, los pusiste a prueba y descubriste que eran falsos.
es.R: Sé todo lo que haces. Sé lo mucho que trabajas y cómo sigues adelante. Sé que no toleras a la gente mala. Algunos decían que eran apóstoles, pero no lo eran. Tú los pusiste a prueba y descubriste que mentían.

sw.L: Najua matendo yako, kazi yako ngumu na uvumilivu wako, na kwamba huwezi kuwastahimili watu waovu; tena uliwapima wale wanaojiita mitume ilhali si mitume, ukagundua kwamba ni waongo.
sw.B: Najua matendo yako, jinsi ulivyojitaabisha katika kazi na jinsi ulivyovumilia. Najua kwamba huwezi kuwastahimili watu wanaotenda maovu. Wale wanaojiita mitume, ingawa sio, uliwapima ukagundua kuwa ni waongo.
sw.R: Najua kila kitu unachofanya. Najua jinsi unavyofanya kazi kwa bidii na jinsi unavyoendelea bila kukata tamaa. Najua kwamba hukubali kukaa na watu waovu. Watu fulani walisema kuwa wao ni mitume, lakini hawakuwa mitume. Uliwapima, ukagundua kwamba walikuwa waongo.

vi.L: Ta biết các việc làm của con, sự lao khổ và sự kiên trì của con, và [biết] con không thể chịu đựng những kẻ ác, và con đã thử những kẻ tự xưng là sứ đồ mà không phải là sứ đồ, và con đã thấy họ là giả dối.
vi.B: Ta biết các việc làm của con, biết con đã lao khổ và kiên trì thế nào. Ta biết con không thể dung thứ những kẻ làm ác. Những kẻ tự xưng là sứ đồ mà không phải là sứ đồ, con đã thử họ và thấy họ là giả dối.
vi.R: Ta biết mọi việc con làm. Ta biết con làm việc khó nhọc thế nào và con đã kiên trì ra sao. Ta biết con không chấp nhận những kẻ gian ác. Có những người tự xưng là sứ đồ, nhưng không phải. Con đã thử họ và thấy họ nói dối.

ko.L: 나는 네 행위들과 수고와 인내를 안다. 또 네가 악한 사람들을 견디지 못하는 것과, 사도가 아니면서 스스로 사도라고 하는 사람들을 시험하여 그들이 거짓말쟁이라는 것을 밝혀낸 것도 안다.
ko.B: 나는 네 행위를 안다. 네가 얼마나 수고하였고 얼마나 인내하였는지 안다. 또 나는 네가 악한 사람들을 참지 못한다는 것을 안다. 너는 사도가 아니면서 스스로 사도라고 하는 사람들을 시험하여 그들이 거짓되다는 것을 밝혀냈다.
ko.R: 나는 네가 하는 모든 일을 안다. 네가 얼마나 열심히 일하고 얼마나 끝까지 견디는지 안다. 나는 네가 악한 사람들을 그냥 두지 않는다는 것을 안다. 어떤 사람들은 자기들이 사도라고 했지만 사도가 아니었다. 너는 그들을 시험하여 그들이 거짓말을 하고 있다는 것을 알아냈다.

decisions.choice: your works: what you do, your whole way of life
decisions.reason: ἔργα is a broad word for deeds and conduct. Each letter begins "I know" (2:2, 9, 13, 19; 3:1, 8, 15): the speaker who walks among the churches knows them as they are.

decisions.choice: false apostles: travelling teachers who claimed an apostle's authority
decisions.reason: Apostle means one who is sent. Besides the Twelve and Paul, others were called apostles (Acts 14:14), and travelling teachers who claimed the title came to churches (2 Corinthians 11:13; 1 John 4:1). Paul had warned the Ephesian elders that false teachers would come (Acts 20:29-30). The church at Ephesus tested such people and found them false.

decisions.choice: cannot bear: cannot tolerate evil people among them
decisions.reason: βαστάσαι means to carry or bear. Here, with evil people as its object, it means to put up with them. The same verb comes back in 2:3 in its other sense: they have borne hardship for Christ's name.

decisions.choice: Those who call themselves apostles ... you put to the test (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the false apostles first so that the clause "though they are not" stays next to their claim.

decisions.choice: "tu" for the church addressed in each message; "vous" where the Greek turns to the plural (2:10, 2:13, 2:23-25) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: Each message speaks to the church, through its angel, in the singular, and French follows the Greek number as the style guide asks (section 6). Where the Greek turns to the plural to speak to the members, French says "vous", so the shift the Greek makes stays visible.

decisions.choice: Conozco tus obras (L, B); Sé todo lo que haces (R)
decisions.reason: "Obras" names a person's whole way of acting, as the meaning decision says, and Literal and Balanced keep the word, which recurs in every letter. Readable turns it into a plain verb, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kuwastahimili (2:2); umestahimili (2:3)
decisions.reason: One verb, "kustahimili" (to bear), for both places, so that the play on words survives: they cannot bear evil people, yet they have borne hardship (m1 in 2:3). "Uvumilivu" stays for endurance.

decisions.choice: "Ta biết các việc làm của con" (L, B); "Ta biết mọi việc con làm" (R), the same words in each letter (2:2, 2:19; 3:1, 3:8, 3:15)
decisions.reason: "Your works" is the whole way of life (m1), and the sentence returns in five letters, so it keeps one form at each level. The sentence begins with "Ta", which takes no span at the start of a sentence.

decisions.choice: "나는 네 행위들을 안다" (L), "나는 네 행위를 안다" (B), "나는 네가 하는 모든 일을 안다" (R), in each letter (2:2, 19; 3:1, 8, 15)
decisions.reason: Your works are what you do, your whole way of life (meaning decision); each level keeps one wording for the refrain, so the letters can be compared.

source.text: καὶ ὑπομονὴν ἔχεις, καὶ ἐβάστασας διὰ τὸ ὄνομά μου, καὶ οὐ κεκοπίακες.

records.literal_gloss: and endurance you have, and you bore on account of the name of me, and not you have grown weary.

en.L: And you have endurance, and you have borne [up] because of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you have not grown weary.
en.B: You keep going. For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name's sake you have carried heavy loads, and you have not grown tired.
en.R: You keep going and do not give up. You have suffered hard things because you belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you have not become tired of it.

fr.L: Et tu as de la persévérance, et tu as supporté [bien des choses] à cause de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et tu ne t’es pas lassé.
fr.B: Tu persévères. À cause de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, tu as porté de lourds fardeaux, et tu ne t’es pas lassé.
fr.R: Tu tiens bon et tu n’abandonnes pas. Tu as souffert des choses difficiles parce que tu {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}appartiens, et tu ne t’es pas découragé.

es.L: Y tienes perseverancia, y has soportado [cargas] por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y no te has cansado.
es.B: Sigues firme. Por causa de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre has llevado cargas pesadas, y no te has cansado.
es.R: Sigues adelante y no te rindes. Has sufrido cosas difíciles porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} perteneces, y no te has cansado.

sw.L: Nawe una uvumilivu, na umestahimili kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}}, wala hujachoka.
sw.B: Unaendelea kuvumilia. Kwa ajili ya jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} umestahimili mizigo mizito, wala hujachoka.
sw.R: Unaendelea kuvumilia, wala hukati tamaa. Umestahimili mambo magumu kwa sababu wewe ni {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, wala hujachoka.

vi.L: Và con có sự kiên trì, và con đã chịu đựng vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và con đã không mỏi mệt.
vi.B: Con vẫn kiên trì. Vì danh {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, con đã mang những gánh nặng, và con đã không mỏi mệt.
vi.R: Con cứ kiên trì và không bỏ cuộc. Con đã chịu những điều khó khăn vì con thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và con đã không mệt mỏi.

ko.L: 너는 인내하고 있고, 내 이름 때문에 견디었으며, 지치지 않았다.
ko.B: 너는 끝까지 견디고 있다. 너는 내 이름 때문에 무거운 짐을 지고도 지치지 않았다.
ko.R: 너는 포기하지 않고 계속 견디고 있다. 너는 나에게 속해 있기 때문에 어려운 일을 겪었지만, 그 일에 지치지 않았다.

decisions.choice: plays on words: they bear hardship though they cannot bear evil; they labor and have not grown weary
decisions.reason: ἐβάστασας repeats the verb of 2:2, "bear": they cannot bear evil people, yet they have borne hardship. κεκοπίακες is from the same root as "labor" in 2:2: they have labored, and the labor has not worn them out.

decisions.choice: because of my name: because they belong to Jesus and bear his name
decisions.reason: A name stands for the person. To suffer for his name is to suffer because one is known as his (Acts 5:41; Matthew 10:22).

decisions.choice: because you belong to me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "my name" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: "tu as supporté" (L), echoing "tu ne peux pas supporter" in 2:2
decisions.reason: The Greek plays on one verb: they cannot bear evil people, yet they have borne hardship for Christ's name (m1). French "supporter" covers both senses, so Literal keeps the play with one verb; Balanced and Readable say what was borne.

decisions.choice: has soportado (L); has llevado cargas pesadas (B); has sufrido cosas difíciles (R)
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 2:2 for bearing evil people, which they cannot do, and here for bearing hardship, which they have done. Spanish "soportar" can do both at Literal, keeping the wordplay; Balanced and Readable spell out what was carried.

source.text: ἀλλὰ ἔχω κατὰ σοῦ ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην σου τὴν πρώτην ἀφῆκες.

records.literal_gloss: But I have against you that the love of you the first you left.

en.L: But I have [this] against you, that you have left your first love.
en.B: But here is my complaint against you: the love you had in the beginning, you have let go.
en.R: But there is one thing I have against you. You have stopped loving the way you loved at the beginning.

fr.L: Mais j’ai [ceci] contre toi : tu as abandonné ton premier amour.
fr.B: Mais voici ce que je te reproche : l’amour que tu avais au début, tu l’as laissé.
fr.R: Mais il y a une chose que je te reproche. Tu n’aimes plus comme tu aimais au commencement.

es.L: Pero tengo [esto] contra ti: que has dejado tu primer amor.
es.B: Pero tengo una queja contra ti: el amor que tenías al principio lo has abandonado.
es.R: Pero hay una cosa que tengo contra ti. Ya no amas como amabas al principio.

sw.L: Lakini ninalo [hili] dhidi yako: kwamba upendo wako wa kwanza umeuacha.
sw.B: Lakini hili ndilo ninalokulaumu: ule upendo uliokuwa nao mwanzoni umeuacha.
sw.R: Lakini kuna jambo moja ninalokulaumu. Umeacha kupenda jinsi ulivyopenda mwanzoni.

vi.L: Nhưng Ta có [điều này] trách con: con đã bỏ tình yêu thương ban đầu của con.
vi.B: Nhưng đây là điều Ta trách con: tình yêu thương con có lúc ban đầu, con đã bỏ đi.
vi.R: Nhưng có một điều Ta trách con. Con đã thôi yêu thương như con đã yêu thương lúc ban đầu.

ko.L: 그러나 나에게는 너를 나무랄 것이 있다. 네가 처음 사랑을 버렸다는 것이다.
ko.B: 그러나 나는 너를 책망할 것이 있다. 너는 처음에 가졌던 사랑을 버렸다.
ko.R: 그러나 너에게 한 가지 나무랄 것이 있다. 너는 처음에 사랑하던 것처럼 사랑하기를 그만두었다.

decisions.choice: the first love: the love they had at first, and the love that should come first
decisions.reason: πρώτην means first in time, and here it points back to the church's early days, as "the first works" do in 2:5. It may also carry the sense of what comes first in importance.

decisions.choice: love for Christ and love for one another, which the text does not separate
decisions.reason: The text does not say whom they have stopped loving. In John's writings love for God and love for fellow believers go together (1 John 4:20-21). A church that tests and rejects false teachers can grow hard toward its own members, and that may be the danger here. The object is left unstated.

decisions.choice: left behind: abandoned, not merely cooled
decisions.reason: ἀφῆκες means to let go or leave. The love is not said to have weakened but to have been left behind, which is why 2:5 calls for repentance.

decisions.choice: "tình yêu thương ban đầu"
decisions.reason: The first love is the love they had at first, and the love that should come first (m1); the meaning decision does not separate love for Christ and for one another (m2), so Vietnamese uses "tình yêu thương", which can hold both.

decisions.choice: "나에게는 너를 나무랄 것이 있다" (L), "나는 너를 책망할 것이 있다" (B), "너에게 ... 나무랄 것이 있다" (R) for "I have against you", in 2:4, 14, 20
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom means "I hold this against you", which Korean says with "나무라다" (find fault); a word-for-word "against" would sound like enmity.

source.text: μνημόνευε οὖν πόθεν πέπτωκας, καὶ μετανόησον καὶ τὰ πρῶτα ἔργα ποίησον· εἰ δὲ μή, ἔρχομαί σοι, καὶ κινήσω τὴν λυχνίαν σου ἐκ τοῦ τόπου αὐτῆς, ἐὰν μὴ μετανοήσῃς.

records.literal_gloss: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and the first works do; but if not, I am coming to you and I will move the lampstand of you out of the place of it, if not you repent.

en.L: Remember, then, from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works. But if not, I am coming to you, and I will move your lampstand out of its place, unless you repent.
en.B: So call to mind the height you have fallen from. Repent, and act as you did at the start. Otherwise I am coming to you, and I will move your lampstand from where it stands, unless you repent.
en.R: So remember what you were like before you fell. Turn away from your sins and do the things you did at first. If you do not, I will come to you and take your lampstand away from its place. That will happen unless you change.

fr.L: Souviens-toi donc d’où tu es tombé, et repens-toi, et fais les premières œuvres. Sinon, je viens à toi, et j’ôterai ton chandelier de sa place, si tu ne te repens pas.
fr.B: Rappelle-toi donc de quelle hauteur tu es tombé. Repens-toi, et agis comme au commencement. Sinon, je viens à toi, et j’enlèverai ton chandelier de la place où il se tient, à moins que tu ne te repentes.
fr.R: Alors souviens-toi de ce que tu étais avant de tomber. Détourne-toi de tes péchés et fais ce que tu faisais au début. Sinon, je viendrai vers toi et j’enlèverai ton chandelier de sa place. Cela arrivera si tu ne changes pas.

es.L: Recuerda, pues, de dónde has caído, y arrepiéntete y haz las primeras obras; y si no, vengo a ti y quitaré tu candelabro de su lugar, si no te arrepientes.
es.B: Así que recuerda desde qué altura has caído. Arrepiéntete y vuelve a actuar como al principio. Si no, vengo a ti y quitaré tu candelabro de su sitio, a menos que te arrepientas.
es.R: Así que recuerda cómo eras antes de caer. Apártate de tus pecados y haz lo que hacías al principio. Si no lo haces, vendré a ti y quitaré tu candelabro de su lugar. Eso sucederá si no cambias.

sw.L: Basi kumbuka umeanguka kutoka wapi, ukatubu, ukafanye matendo ya kwanza. La sivyo, ninakuja kwako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakiondoa kinara chako cha taa mahali pake, usipotubu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo kumbuka umeanguka kutoka juu kiasi gani. Tubu, ukatende kama ulivyotenda mwanzoni. La sivyo, ninakuja kwako, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakiondoa kinara chako cha taa mahali kilipo, usipotubu.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo kumbuka jinsi ulivyokuwa kabla hujaanguka. Acha dhambi zako, ukafanye mambo uliyoyafanya mwanzoni. Usipofanya hivyo, nitakuja kwako na kukiondoa kinara chako cha taa mahali pake. Hilo litatokea usipobadilika.

vi.L: Vậy hãy nhớ lại con đã sa ngã từ đâu, hãy ăn năn và làm lại những việc ban đầu; nếu không, Ta sẽ đến với con và dời chân đèn của con khỏi chỗ của nó, nếu con không ăn năn.
vi.B: Vậy hãy nhớ lại con đã sa ngã từ độ cao nào. Hãy ăn năn và làm những việc như con đã làm lúc ban đầu. Nếu không, Ta sẽ đến với con và dời chân đèn của con khỏi chỗ của nó, trừ khi con ăn năn.
vi.R: Vậy hãy nhớ lại con đã như thế nào trước khi sa ngã. Hãy từ bỏ tội lỗi và làm những việc con đã làm lúc đầu. Nếu con không làm vậy, Ta sẽ đến với con và cất chân đèn của con khỏi chỗ của nó. Điều đó sẽ xảy ra nếu con không thay đổi.

ko.L: 그러므로 네가 어디에서 떨어졌는지 기억하고, 회개하여 처음 행위들을 하여라. 그렇지 않으면 내가 너에게 가서, 네가 회개하지 않는 한, 네 등잔대를 그 자리에서 옮길 것이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 네가 얼마나 높은 데서 떨어졌는지 기억하여라. 회개하고 처음에 하던 일을 하여라. 그렇지 않으면 내가 너에게 가겠다. 네가 회개하지 않으면, 나는 네 등잔대를 그 자리에서 옮겨 버릴 것이다.
ko.R: 그러므로 네가 넘어지기 전에 어떠했는지 기억하여라. 죄에서 돌아서서 처음에 하던 일을 하여라. 그렇게 하지 않으면 내가 너에게 가서 네 등잔대를 그 자리에서 치워 버릴 것이다. 네가 변하지 않으면 그 일이 일어날 것이다.

decisions.choice: repent: turn around in mind and life
decisions.reason: μετανόησον means to change one's mind, and in the Bible it means turning from sin to God in thought and action. The command is in a form that calls for a decisive turn. Repentance is a call in five of the seven letters (2:5, 16, 21-22; 3:3, 19).

decisions.choice: removing the lampstand: the church would cease to be a church that bears his light
alternatives: the city's church would be moved elsewhere
decisions.reason: The lampstands are the churches (1:20). To move a lampstand from its place is to end that church's existence as a church, or its place as a light among the churches. The threat is about the church as a body, not about each believer's salvation.

decisions.choice: I am coming to you: a coming in judgment on this church
decisions.reason: "I am coming" is present, with a future sense. Here it is conditional ("if not") and aimed at one church, so it is most likely a visit of judgment within history, not the final coming, which does not depend on whether Ephesus repents. Revelation also speaks of the final coming in the same words (22:7, 20).

decisions.choice: repent (L, B); turn away from your sins, change (R)
decisions.reason: "Repent" is the familiar word and is kept at Literal and Balanced. Readable says what it means in plain words.

decisions.choice: "se repentir" (L, B); "se détourner de ses péchés", "changer" (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and the English: the familiar word stays at Literal and Balanced, and Readable says in plain words what turning around in mind and life means (m1).

decisions.choice: arrepiéntete (L, B); apártate de tus pecados, cambia (R)
decisions.reason: "Arrepentirse" is the settled word for the Greek verb in the Spanish New Testament. Readable says what it means in plain words, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: tubu (L, B); acha dhambi zako ... usipobadilika (R)
decisions.reason: "Kutubu" for repent, as in the Gospels and Acts; Readable says "acha dhambi zako" (turn away from your sins), as Mark and Matthew do at Readable. The same in the other letters.

decisions.choice: "ăn năn" (L, B); "từ bỏ tội lỗi", "thay đổi" (R) for repent, through the letters
decisions.reason: "Ăn năn" is the Protestant word for repentance, as in the Vietnamese Romans (2:4) and 2 Peter (3:9), a turning of the whole life (m1); Readable says what it is, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "회개하다" (L, B); "죄에서 돌아서다", "변하다" (R) for repent, through the book
decisions.reason: Repentance is turning around in mind and life (meaning decision). "회개" is the Korean Gospels' word (Matthew 3:8); Readable says it in plain words, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ἀλλὰ τοῦτο ἔχεις ὅτι μισεῖς τὰ ἔργα τῶν Νικολαϊτῶν, ἃ κἀγὼ μισῶ.

records.literal_gloss: But this you have, that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.

en.L: But you have this: that you hate the works of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
en.B: Yet there is this to your credit: you hate the things the Nicolaitans do, and so do I.
en.R: But you do one thing that is good. You hate what the Nicolaitans do. I hate it too.

fr.L: Mais tu as ceci : tu hais les œuvres des Nicolaïtes, que je hais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi.
fr.B: Pourtant, il y a ceci en ta faveur : tu détestes ce que font les Nicolaïtes, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi.
fr.R: Mais tu fais une chose qui est bonne. Tu détestes ce que font les Nicolaïtes. Moi aussi, je le déteste.

es.L: Pero tienes esto: que aborreces las obras de los nicolaítas, las cuales yo también aborrezco.
es.B: Pero algo hay a tu favor: aborreces lo que hacen los nicolaítas, y yo también lo aborrezco.
es.R: Pero haces una cosa buena. Odias lo que hacen los nicolaítas. Yo también lo odio.

sw.L: Lakini hili unalo, kwamba unayachukia matendo ya Wanikolai, ambayo {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} pia nayachukia.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, una jambo hili jema: unayachukia mambo wanayoyafanya Wanikolai, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} pia nayachukia.
sw.R: Lakini unafanya jambo moja jema. Unachukia mambo wanayoyafanya Wanikolai. Mimi pia nayachukia.

vi.L: Nhưng con có điều này: con ghét các việc làm của phái Ni-cô-la, là điều Ta cũng ghét.
vi.B: Tuy vậy, con có điều này đáng khen: con ghét những việc phái Ni-cô-la làm, và Ta cũng ghét những việc ấy.
vi.R: Nhưng con có một điều tốt. Con ghét những việc phái Ni-cô-la làm. Ta cũng ghét những việc ấy.

ko.L: 그러나 너에게는 이것이 있다. 네가 니골라당의 행위들을 미워한다는 것이다. 나도 그것을 미워한다.
ko.B: 그러나 너에게는 칭찬할 점이 있다. 너는 니골라당이 하는 일을 미워한다. 나도 그것을 미워한다.
ko.R: 그러나 너는 한 가지 좋은 일을 하고 있다. 너는 니골라당이 하는 일을 미워한다. 나도 그것을 미워한다.

decisions.choice: the Nicolaitans: a group known only from Revelation
decisions.reason: The New Testament names the Nicolaitans only here and in 2:15, where their teaching is set beside Balaam's: eating food sacrificed to idols and sexual immorality (2:14). Some early Christian writers connected them with Nicolaus of Antioch (Acts 6:5), but that link cannot be confirmed. The letter does not describe them further.

decisions.choice: it is what they do that is hated
decisions.reason: The object of the hatred is ἔργα, the works, not the people. The church shares the hatred of the one who speaks.

decisions.choice: los nicolaítas
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish form of the group's name. Nothing more is known of them than Revelation says, so no level explains the name.

decisions.choice: Wanikolai
decisions.reason: The group's name (m1) with the Swahili prefix for a people or party, as "Mafarisayo" and "Masadukayo" take theirs. The same in 2:15.

decisions.choice: "phái Ni-cô-la" for the Nicolaitans
decisions.reason: The Nicolaitans were a group known only from Revelation (m1); "phái" names a party or sect, and "người Ni-cô-la" would sound like a people or a nationality.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] having an ear let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

en.L: The one who has an ear, let {{gender:that person|him}} hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
en.B: Whoever has ears should listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.
en.R: Everyone who can hear should listen carefully to what the Spirit is saying to the churches.

fr.L: Que celui qui a une oreille entende ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises.
fr.B: Que celui qui a des oreilles écoute ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises.
fr.R: Que tous ceux qui peuvent entendre écoutent bien ce que l’Esprit dit aux églises.

es.L: El que tiene oído, que oiga lo que el Espíritu dice a las iglesias.
es.B: Quien tenga oídos, que escuche lo que el Espíritu está diciendo a las iglesias.
es.R: Todo el que pueda oír, que escuche con atención lo que el Espíritu está diciendo a las iglesias.

sw.L: Aliye na sikio, na asikie kile Roho anachoyaambia makanisa.
sw.B: Kila mwenye masikio na asikilize kile Roho anachoyaambia makanisa.
sw.R: Kila anayeweza kusikia na asikilize kwa makini kile Roho anachoyaambia makanisa.

vi.L: Ai có tai, hãy nghe điều Thánh Linh phán với các Hội Thánh.
vi.B: Ai có tai thì hãy lắng nghe điều Thánh Linh đang phán với các Hội Thánh.
vi.R: Ai nghe được thì hãy chú ý lắng nghe điều Thánh Linh đang nói với các Hội Thánh.

ko.L: 귀가 있는 사람은 성령께서 교회들에게 하시는 말씀을 들어라.
ko.B: 귀가 있는 사람은 성령께서 교회들에게 하시는 말씀을 잘 들어라.
ko.R: 들을 수 있는 사람은 누구나 성령께서 교회들에게 하시는 말씀을 귀 기울여 들어라.

decisions.choice: an echo of Jesus's saying in the Gospels: whoever has ears, let them hear
decisions.reason: Jesus closes parables with these words in the Gospels (Matthew 11:15; 13:9, 43; Mark 4:9). They call for more than hearing sounds: the hearer is to take the message in and act on it. Each of the seven letters ends with the call (2:7, 11, 17, 29; 3:6, 13, 22), and 13:9 repeats it.

decisions.choice: the Spirit speaks the risen Jesus's words, and each letter is for every church
decisions.reason: The letter is spoken by the risen Jesus (2:1), yet the call says it is what the Spirit says. The words of Christ come to the churches through the Spirit, as John was "in the Spirit" when he heard them (1:10). "Churches" is plural: what is written to one church is meant for all seven, and for every church that hears it.

decisions.choice: The one who has an ear, let that person hear (L); Whoever has ears should listen (B, R)
alternatives: He who has an ear, let him hear
decisions.reason: The Greek uses a masculine form for anyone at all. Literal keeps the form with a gender setting; Balanced and Readable use "whoever" and "everyone", which need no setting. English says "ears" where the Greek has the singular.

decisions.choice: "Que celui qui a une oreille entende", with no gender span (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The English Literal needs a gender span on "him". French "celui qui" is already generic, as the style guide says (section 7), so the sentence needs no setting; the same holds for "celui qui est vainqueur ... je lui donnerai" in each message.

decisions.choice: El que tiene oído, que oiga (L); Quien tenga oídos, que escuche (B); Todo el que pueda oír, que escuche con atención (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish "el que" and "quien" already take in men and women, and the third-person command "que oiga" has no pronoun, so no gender span is needed where the English Literal has one. The same three wordings close every letter.

decisions.choice: no gender span
alternatives: a gender span, as in the English
decisions.reason: Swahili "aliye na" and "kila mwenye" (whoever has) are already free of gender, so the English span "that person|him" has no Swahili counterpart. The same call closes all seven letters.

decisions.choice: the closing call of every letter: "Ai có tai, hãy nghe điều Thánh Linh phán với các Hội Thánh" (L), "Ai có tai thì hãy lắng nghe ..." (B), "Ai nghe được thì hãy chú ý lắng nghe điều Thánh Linh đang nói ..." (R); no gender span
decisions.reason: The call echoes Jesus's saying in the Gospels (m1), so it keeps the Vietnamese Matthew's words (11:15) and is repeated unchanged in all seven letters. The Spirit speaks as God (m2), so Literal and Balanced say "phán", as the Vietnamese 1 Timothy does (4:1), and Readable "nói", as there. "Ai" already includes everyone, so the English that person/him setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: the closing call of each letter in one wording per level, built on the Korean Matthew 11:15 ("귀가 있는 사람은 들어라" L, "... 잘 들어라" B); "사람" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English Literal
decisions.reason: The call echoes Jesus's saying in the Gospels (meaning decision), so the Korean takes up the Korean Gospels' wording, and it is repeated word for word at each level in all seven letters (2:7, 11, 17, 29; 3:6, 13, 22). Korean "사람" already means anyone, so the gender setting has nothing to change.

source.text: τῷ νικῶντι δώσω αὐτῷ φαγεῖν ἐκ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: To the [one] overcoming I will give to him to eat from the tree of the life, which is in the paradise of the God.

en.L: To the one who overcomes, to {{gender:that person|him}} I will give [the right] to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God."
en.B: I will let everyone who overcomes eat from the tree of life that grows in God's paradise."
en.R: I will let everyone who wins the victory eat from the tree of life, which grows in God's garden, paradise."

fr.L: À celui qui est vainqueur, à lui je donnerai [le droit] de manger de l’arbre de la vie, qui est dans le paradis de Dieu. »
fr.B: Je permettrai à tout vainqueur de manger de l’arbre de vie qui pousse dans le paradis de Dieu. »
fr.R: Je permettrai à tous ceux qui remportent la victoire de manger de l’arbre de vie, qui pousse dans le jardin de Dieu, le paradis. »

es.L: Al que venza, le daré [el derecho] de comer del árbol de la vida, que está en el paraíso de Dios».
es.B: A todo el que venza le daré a comer del árbol de la vida que crece en el paraíso de Dios».
es.R: A todo el que gane la victoria le dejaré comer del árbol de la vida, que crece en el jardín de Dios, el paraíso».

sw.L: Anayeshinda, nitampa kula kutoka katika mti wa uzima, ulio katika paradiso ya Mungu."
sw.B: Kila anayeshinda nitamruhusu kula matunda ya mti wa uzima ulio katika paradiso ya Mungu."
sw.R: Kila anayepata ushindi nitamruhusu kula matunda ya mti wa uzima, unaoota katika bustani ya Mungu, yaani paradiso."

vi.L: Người nào chiến thắng, Ta sẽ cho người ấy ăn [trái] cây sự sống, là cây ở trong Ba-ra-đi của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.B: Ai chiến thắng, Ta sẽ cho người ấy ăn trái cây sự sống trong Ba-ra-đi của Đức Chúa Trời."
vi.R: Ai chiến thắng, Ta sẽ cho người ấy được ăn trái cây sự sống, là cây mọc trong vườn của Đức Chúa Trời, tức là Ba-ra-đi."

ko.L: 이기는 사람에게는 내가 하나님의 낙원에 있는 생명나무에서 [따서] 먹게 하겠다."
ko.B: 이기는 사람에게는 누구에게나 내가 하나님의 낙원에 있는 생명나무의 열매를 먹게 하겠다."
ko.R: 승리하는 사람에게는 누구에게나 내가 하나님의 동산, 곧 낙원에서 자라는 생명나무의 열매를 먹게 하겠다."

decisions.choice: the one who overcomes: who wins the victory by staying faithful
decisions.reason: νικῶντι means to win or conquer. Each letter ends with a promise to the one who overcomes (2:7, 11, 17, 26; 3:5, 12, 21). In Revelation the victory is won as the Lamb won it, by faithful witness even to death (3:21; 5:5-6; 12:11), not by force.

decisions.choice: the tree of life in the garden of Eden, restored
decisions.reason: The tree of life grew in the garden of Eden (Genesis 2:9), and after their disobedience the man and the woman were kept from it (Genesis 3:22-24). παραδείσῳ was a word for a garden or park, and the Greek Old Testament uses it for Eden. The promise is that what was lost will be given back; Revelation 22:2, 14 shows the tree again in the new Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: to the one who overcomes, to that person (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek names the person and then repeats him with αὐτῷ, "to him". English does not need both, so only Literal shows the repetition, here and in 2:17 and 2:26.

decisions.choice: overcomes (L, B); wins the victory (R)
decisions.reason: "Overcome" says winning through against opposition, and suits a victory won by endurance (m1). Readable uses plain words.

decisions.choice: "celui qui est vainqueur", "tout vainqueur" (L, B); "ceux qui remportent la victoire" (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The Greek is a present participle: one who wins through, whose victory is won by staying faithful (m1). "Vainqueur" says this in current French; the traditional future "celui qui vaincra" turns it into a later event. Readable uses plain words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: el que venza (L, B); el que gane la victoria (R)
decisions.reason: "Vencer" is the verb the Spanish 1 John uses for overcoming the world, and it is kept at Literal and Balanced in every letter and through the book. Readable says "ganar la victoria", as the English Readable says "wins the victory".

decisions.choice: anayeshinda (L, B); anayepata ushindi (R)
decisions.reason: "Kushinda" (to win, to overcome), as in 1 John 5:4-5, for the one who wins by staying faithful (m1); the same in each of the seven letters.

decisions.choice: kula matunda ya mti
decisions.reason: Swahili eats the fruit of a tree, not "from" the tree; Balanced and Readable say "matunda" (fruit), which the Greek implies. Literal keeps "kutoka katika mti".

decisions.choice: "Người nào chiến thắng" (L), "Ai chiến thắng" (B, R) for "the one who overcomes" in every letter and in 21:7; "chiến thắng" for this verb through the book
decisions.reason: The one who overcomes wins the victory by staying faithful (m1). "Chiến thắng" is the Vietnamese Romans' word for winning (8:37), and the same form opens the promise in all seven letters; "người ấy" follows, with no gender span, since Vietnamese "người" includes everyone. "Ba-ra-đi" is the Vietnamese Luke's form for paradise (23:43), and "cây sự sống" the tree of life (m2).

decisions.choice: "이기는 사람" (L, B); "승리하는 사람" (R) for the one who overcomes, in every letter and in 21:7
decisions.reason: The one who overcomes is the one who wins the victory by staying faithful (meaning decision). "이기다" is the verb of the Korean John 16:33 and 1 John 5:4-5 for the same Greek verb; Readable says "win the victory", as the English Readable does. "사람" (not "자") keeps the phrase in current Korean.

source.text: Καὶ τῷ ἀγγέλῳ τῆς ἐν Σμύρνῃ ἐκκλησίας γράψον· Τάδε λέγει ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, ὃς ἐγένετο νεκρὸς καὶ ἔζησεν·

sw.B: Kwa malaika wa kanisa la Smirna, andika: "Huu ndio ujumbe wa yule aliye wa kwanza na wa mwisho, aliyekufa akawa hai tena:

vi.B: Hãy viết cho thiên sứ của Hội Thánh tại Si-miệc-nơ: "Đây là lời của Đấng Đầu Tiên và Cuối Cùng, Đấng đã chết và đã sống lại:
vi.R: Hãy viết thư này cho thiên sứ của Hội Thánh tại Si-miệc-nơ: "Sứ điệp này đến từ Đấng Đầu Tiên và Cuối Cùng, Đấng đã chết và đã sống lại.

ko.L: 서머나에 있는 교회의 천사에게 써라. "처음이요 마지막이시며, 죽으셨다가 살아나신 분이 이것들을 말씀하신다.
ko.B: 서머나 교회의 천사에게 이렇게 써라. "처음이요 마지막이시며, 죽으셨다가 다시 살아나신 분이 이렇게 말씀하신다.
ko.R: 서머나에 있는 교회의 천사에게 이 편지를 써라. "이것은 처음이요 마지막이시며, 죽으셨다가 다시 살아나신 분이 보내시는 말씀이다.

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the titles from 1:17-18
decisions.reason: The speaker is described with his own words from 1:17-18. To a church facing prison and death (2:10), he speaks as the one who died and lives.

decisions.choice: Smyrna: a wealthy port north of Ephesus, long loyal to Rome
decisions.reason: Smyrna (modern Izmir) was a large and prosperous city that had built a temple to the goddess Roma and later one to the emperor Tiberius. Its church was poor and under pressure (2:9).

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

source.text: Οἶδά σου τὴν θλῖψιν καὶ τὴν πτωχείαν, ἀλλὰ πλούσιος εἶ, καὶ τὴν βλασφημίαν ἐκ τῶν λεγόντων Ἰουδαίους εἶναι ἑαυτούς, καὶ οὐκ εἰσίν, ἀλλὰ συναγωγὴ τοῦ Σατανᾶ.

records.literal_gloss: I know of you the affliction and the poverty—but rich you are—and the slander from those saying Jews to be themselves, and not they are, but a synagogue of the Satan.

en.L: I know your affliction and poverty—but you are rich—and the slander of those who say they are Jews and are not, but [are] a synagogue of Satan.
en.B: I know your affliction and your poverty—though in fact you are rich—and the abuse you receive from those who claim to be Jews but are not. They are Satan's synagogue.
en.R: I know about your troubles and that you are poor. But really you are rich! I know that some people say evil things about you. They say they are Jews, but they are not. Their meeting place belongs to Satan.

fr.L: Je connais ta détresse et ta pauvreté — mais tu es riche — et la calomnie de ceux qui se disent juifs et ne le sont pas, mais [sont] une synagogue de Satan.
fr.B: Je connais ta détresse et ta pauvreté — pourtant tu es riche — et les injures que tu subis de la part de ceux qui prétendent être juifs mais ne le sont pas. Ils sont la synagogue de Satan.
fr.R: Je connais tes souffrances, et je sais que tu es pauvre. Mais en réalité, tu es riche ! Je sais que des gens disent du mal de toi. Ils disent qu’ils sont juifs, mais ce n’est pas vrai. Leur lieu de réunion appartient à Satan.

es.L: Conozco tu aflicción y tu pobreza —pero eres rico— y la calumnia de los que dicen ser judíos, y no lo son, sino [que son] una sinagoga de Satanás.
es.B: Conozco tu aflicción y tu pobreza —aunque en realidad eres rico— y los insultos que recibes de los que dicen ser judíos y no lo son. Son la sinagoga de Satanás.
es.R: Sé de tus sufrimientos y sé que eres pobre. ¡Pero en realidad eres rico! Sé que algunos hablan mal de ti. Dicen que son judíos, pero no lo son. Su lugar de reunión pertenece a Satanás.

sw.L: Najua dhiki yako na umaskini wako—lakini wewe ni tajiri—na kashfa ya wale wanaosema kwamba wao ni Wayahudi nao sio, bali ni sinagogi la Shetani.
sw.B: Najua dhiki yako na umaskini wako, ingawa kwa kweli wewe ni tajiri. Najua pia matusi unayotukanwa na wale wanaojidai kuwa Wayahudi ilhali sio. Wao ni sinagogi la Shetani.
sw.R: Najua taabu zako, na kwamba wewe ni maskini. Lakini kwa kweli wewe ni tajiri! Najua kwamba watu fulani wanakusema vibaya. Wanasema kuwa wao ni Wayahudi, lakini sio. Mahali pao pa kukutania ni pa Shetani.

vi.L: Ta biết hoạn nạn và sự nghèo khó của con, nhưng con giàu có, và [Ta biết] lời vu khống của những kẻ tự xưng là người Do Thái mà không phải, nhưng [là] nhà hội của Sa-tan.
vi.B: Ta biết hoạn nạn và sự nghèo khó của con, dù thật ra con giàu có. Ta biết những lời vu khống con phải chịu từ những kẻ tự xưng là người Do Thái mà không phải. Họ là nhà hội của Sa-tan.
vi.R: Ta biết những khó khăn của con và biết con nghèo. Nhưng thật ra con giàu có! Ta biết có những người nói xấu con. Họ tự xưng là người Do Thái, nhưng không phải. Nơi nhóm họp của họ thuộc về Sa-tan.

ko.L: 나는 네 환난과 가난을 안다. 그러나 너는 부요하다. 또 스스로 유대인이라고 하지만 유대인이 아니라 사탄의 회당인 사람들에게서 [받는] 비방도 [안다].
ko.B: 나는 네 환난과 가난을 안다. 그러나 사실 너는 부요하다. 또 스스로 유대인이라고 하지만 실제로는 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게서 네가 받는 비방도 안다. 그들은 사탄의 회당이다.
ko.R: 나는 네가 겪는 고난과 네가 가난하다는 것을 안다. 그러나 사실 너는 부자다! 나는 어떤 사람들이 너에 대하여 나쁜 말을 한다는 것도 안다. 그들은 자기들이 유대인이라고 하지만 그렇지 않다. 그들의 모임은 사탄에게 속해 있다.

decisions.choice: rich: rich before God, though poor in money
decisions.reason: The church is poor in the world's terms, perhaps because believers lost work or property, but rich in what counts with God (compare James 2:5). The letter to Laodicea says the reverse (3:17).

decisions.choice: slander: abuse spoken against the believers
decisions.reason: βλασφημίαν can mean speech against God or harmful speech against people. Here it comes from people and falls on the church, so it is slander, perhaps including accusations to the authorities.

decisions.choice: a local group who opposed the church, not the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: John was himself a Jew, and for him the name "Jew" was a name of honor (compare Romans 2:28-29). He says that these particular people in Smyrna, who slander the believers, do not live up to the name, and that in opposing Christ's people they are doing the work of Satan, whose name means "accuser". The words are about one group in one city at one time. They give no ground for hostility toward Jewish people.

decisions.choice: synagogue: a gathering or assembly
decisions.reason: συναγωγὴ means a gathering, and was the usual word for a Jewish congregation and its meeting place. "Synagogue of Satan" turns the word against those who used it of themselves; 3:9 uses the phrase again.

decisions.choice: Their meeting place belongs to Satan (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "synagogue" as a place where people meet; the theology decision says what the phrase does and does not mean.

decisions.choice: la calumnia (L); los insultos que recibes (B)
decisions.reason: The abuse is spoken against the believers, not against God, so "blasfemia" would mislead; "calumnia" is the settled word for this sense of the Greek word.

decisions.choice: sinagogi la Shetani
decisions.reason: "Sinagogi" keeps the Greek word, which means a gathering (m4) and is the name of the Jewish meeting place, as in the Gospels and Acts. Readable says "mahali pao pa kukutania" (their meeting place), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "nhà hội của Sa-tan" (L, B); "nơi nhóm họp của họ thuộc về Sa-tan" (R)
decisions.reason: "Nhà hội" is the style guide's word for a synagogue (m4). The meaning decision reads this as a local group who opposed the church, not the Jewish people as a whole (m3); Vietnamese keeps "những kẻ tự xưng", which limits it to them.

decisions.choice: "사탄의 회당" (L, B); "그들의 모임은 사탄에게 속해 있다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads this as a local group that opposed the church, not the Jewish people as a whole, and footnotes it; "회당" (synagogue, gathering) is the Gospels' word, which Readable explains as a meeting place.

source.text: μηδὲν φοβοῦ ἃ μέλλεις πάσχειν.

records.literal_gloss: Nothing fear what things you are about to suffer.

en.L: Do not fear [any of] the things you are about to suffer.
en.B: Have no fear of anything you are going to suffer.
en.R: Do not be afraid of the suffering that is coming to you.

fr.L: Ne crains rien de ce que tu vas souffrir.
fr.B: N’aie aucune peur de ce que tu vas souffrir.
fr.R: N’aie pas peur des souffrances qui t’attendent.

es.L: No temas nada de lo que vas a padecer.
es.B: No tengas miedo de nada de lo que vas a sufrir.
es.R: No tengas miedo del sufrimiento que te espera.

sw.L: Usiogope chochote kati ya mambo utakayoteseka.
sw.B: Usiogope lolote kati ya mateso yatakayokupata.
sw.R: Usiogope mateso yanayokujia.

vi.L: Đừng sợ [bất cứ] điều gì con sắp phải chịu.
vi.B: Đừng sợ bất cứ điều gì con sắp phải chịu.
vi.R: Đừng sợ những đau khổ sắp đến với con.

ko.L: 네가 받을 고난들을 하나도 두려워하지 마라.
ko.B: 네가 받게 될 어떤 고난도 두려워하지 마라.
ko.R: 너에게 닥쳐올 고난을 두려워하지 마라.

decisions.choice: do not fear anything: a command that also says suffering is coming
decisions.reason: μηδὲν φοβοῦ is emphatic: fear nothing of what lies ahead. The command does not promise that suffering will be avoided; it says that it will come and that they need not fear it.

source.text: ἰδοὺ μέλλει βάλλειν ὁ διάβολος ἐξ ὑμῶν εἰς φυλακὴν ἵνα πειρασθῆτε, καὶ ἕξετε θλῖψιν ἡμερῶν δέκα.

records.literal_gloss: Behold, is about to throw the devil [some] of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction of days ten.

en.L: Look, the devil is about to throw [some] of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have affliction ten days.
en.B: Look: some of you the devil is about to throw into prison, so that you will be tested, and you will face affliction for ten days.
en.R: Listen! The devil will soon have some of you thrown into prison. This will test you. For ten days you will suffer.

fr.L: Voici, le diable va jeter [certains] d’entre vous en prison afin que vous soyez mis à l’épreuve, et vous aurez une détresse de dix jours.
fr.B: Voici : le diable va jeter certains d’entre vous en prison pour vous mettre à l’épreuve, et vous connaîtrez la détresse pendant dix jours.
fr.R: Écoute ! Bientôt, le diable va faire jeter certains d’entre vous en prison. Ce sera une épreuve pour vous. Pendant dix jours, vous allez souffrir.

es.L: Mira, el diablo va a echar [a algunos] de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} en la cárcel para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} probados, y {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} aflicción por diez días.
es.B: Mira: a algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} el diablo los va a echar en la cárcel, para que {{plural_you:sean|seáis}} puestos a prueba, y {{plural_you:pasarán|pasaréis}} aflicción durante diez días.
es.R: ¡Escucha! El diablo pronto hará que metan en la cárcel a algunos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Esto {{plural_you:los|os}} pondrá a prueba. Durante diez días {{plural_you:sufrirán|sufriréis}}.

sw.L: Tazama, Ibilisi yu karibu kuwatupa [baadhi] yenu gerezani ili mjaribiwe, nanyi mtakuwa na dhiki siku kumi.
sw.B: Tazama, Ibilisi anakaribia kuwatupa baadhi yenu gerezani, ili mjaribiwe, nanyi mtapata dhiki kwa siku kumi.
sw.R: Sikiliza! Hivi karibuni Ibilisi atawafanya baadhi yenu watupwe gerezani. Hilo litawajaribu. Mtateseka kwa siku kumi.

vi.L: Kìa, ma quỷ sắp ném [một số] trong các con vào ngục để các con bị thử thách, và các con sẽ bị hoạn nạn mười ngày.
vi.B: Kìa, ma quỷ sắp ném một số người trong các con vào ngục, để các con bị thử thách, và các con sẽ phải chịu hoạn nạn trong mười ngày.
vi.R: Hãy nghe đây! Chẳng bao lâu nữa ma quỷ sẽ khiến một số người trong các con bị bỏ tù. Điều đó sẽ thử thách các con. Các con sẽ chịu khổ trong mười ngày.

ko.L: 보라, 마귀가 너희 가운데 [몇 사람을] 감옥에 던져 넣어 너희를 시험하려고 한다. 너희는 열흘 동안 환난을 당할 것이다.
ko.B: 보라, 마귀가 너희 가운데 몇 사람을 감옥에 던져 넣으려고 한다. 이것은 너희가 시험을 받게 하려는 것이다. 너희는 열흘 동안 환난을 당할 것이다.
ko.R: 잘 들어라! 마귀가 곧 너희 가운데 몇 사람을 감옥에 갇히게 할 것이다. 이것은 너희를 시험할 것이다. 너희는 열흘 동안 고난을 겪을 것이다.

decisions.choice: prison: where people were held before trial or execution
decisions.reason: Roman prisons were mostly a place to hold the accused until they were tried, punished or put to death, not a sentence in themselves. So imprisonment could lead to death, and 2:10 goes on, "be faithful to death".

decisions.choice: tested: put to a trial that shows whether they stand
decisions.reason: πειρασθῆτε can mean to test or to tempt. The devil means harm, but the trial proves their faithfulness. Both senses lie close together, as in Job 1-2.

decisions.choice: ten days: a short time, and a limited one
decisions.reason: Ten days may be a literal span, but it most likely means a short, fixed period that God has set, as in Daniel 1:12-15, where Daniel and his friends are tested for ten days. The suffering is real, and it has an end.

decisions.choice: Look (L, B); Listen (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide does not use "behold". Readable uses "Listen", which calls a young reader to attention in a spoken message.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ... {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} (plural)
decisions.reason: The Greek turns here from the singular "you" of the letter to the plural, the members of the church, so Spanish changes to plural forms with the plural_you span, while "Mira" and the commands before and after stay singular.

source.text: γίνου πιστὸς ἄχρι θανάτου, καὶ δώσω σοι τὸν στέφανον τῆς ζωῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Be faithful until death, and I will give to you the crown of the life.

en.L: Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life.
en.B: Stay faithful even to death, and I will give you the crown of life.
en.R: Stay faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even if it means you must die. Then I will give you the winner's crown, which is life that lasts forever.

fr.L: Sois fidèle jusqu’à la mort, et je te donnerai la couronne de la vie.
fr.B: Reste fidèle jusqu’à la mort, et je te donnerai la couronne de vie.
fr.R: Reste-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} fidèle, même si tu dois mourir. Alors je te donnerai la couronne du vainqueur : la vie qui dure toujours.

es.R: Sigue siendo fiel a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, aunque tengas que morir. Entonces te daré la corona del vencedor, que es la vida que dura para siempre.

sw.L: Kuwa mwaminifu mpaka kifo, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakupa taji la uzima.
sw.B: Dumu katika uaminifu hata kufikia kifo, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakupa taji la uzima.
sw.R: Endelea kuwa mwaminifu {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}, hata kama itakubidi ufe. Kisha nitakupa taji la mshindi, yaani uzima usio na mwisho.

vi.R: Hãy luôn trung tín với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, dù con có phải chết. Rồi Ta sẽ ban cho con mão miện của người chiến thắng, là sự sống đời đời.

ko.L: 죽기까지 신실하여라. 그러면 내가 너에게 생명의 면류관을 주겠다.
ko.B: 죽기까지 신실하여라. 그러면 내가 너에게 생명의 면류관을 주겠다.
ko.R: 죽어야 하더라도 나에게 신실하여라. 그러면 내가 너에게 승리자의 면류관, 곧 영원한 생명을 주겠다.

decisions.choice: until death: to the point of dying, if it comes to that
alternatives: all your life, until you die
decisions.reason: ἄχρι θανάτου can mean up to the end of one's life, but after the warning of prison it most likely means faithful even when faithfulness costs one's life (compare 12:11).

decisions.choice: the crown: the wreath given to a winner
decisions.reason: στέφανον was the wreath of leaves given to the winner of a contest, or to someone honored by a city. It was not a king's crown, for which there is another word (19:12). The promise is the victor's reward.

decisions.choice: the crown that is life
decisions.reason: "Crown of life" most likely means the crown which is life itself: eternal life is the prize (as in James 1:12).

decisions.choice: to me; the winner's crown, which is life that lasts forever (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom they are faithful and explains the picture (m2, m3).

decisions.choice: taji la uzima
decisions.reason: "Taji" takes class 5 agreement ("taji la"), as in James 1:12 and 1 Peter 5:4; it is the winner's wreath (m2).

decisions.choice: "mão miện của sự sống" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The crown is the wreath given to a winner (m2), "mão miện" as in the Vietnamese Philippians (4:1) and James, whose words "mão miện của sự sống" (1:12) Vietnamese keeps. Readable says that the crown is life, as the English Readable does (m3).

decisions.choice: "생명의 면류관"
decisions.reason: The crown is the wreath given to a winner, the crown that is life (meaning decision), worded as in the Korean James 1:12, which has the same phrase.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων οὖς ἀκουσάτω τί τὸ πνεῦμα λέγει ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις.

decisions.choice: the call that closes every letter
decisions.reason: The same call ends each of the seven letters; see the notes on 2:7. What the risen Jesus says to one church, the Spirit says to all of them.

en.B: The second death will never harm anyone who overcomes."
en.R: Everyone who wins the victory will be safe from the second death. It will never hurt them."

es.B: La segunda muerte jamás dañará a quien venza».
es.R: Todo el que gane la victoria estará a salvo de la segunda muerte. Nunca le hará daño».

sw.R: Kila anayepata ushindi atakuwa salama mbali na kifo cha pili. Hakitamdhuru kamwe."

decisions.choice: the second death: final judgment, after the death of the body
decisions.reason: Revelation explains the phrase itself: the second death is the lake of fire (20:14; 21:8), and it has no power over those who share in the first resurrection (20:6). Believers in Smyrna may die the first death (2:10), but not the second.

decisions.choice: "sự chết thứ hai" (also 20:6, 20:14; 21:8)

decisions.choice: these things says: the formula of a prophet bringing the Lord's word
decisions.reason: Τάδε λέγει recalls the prophets' "Thus says the LORD", which the Greek Old Testament renders with the same words. Each of the seven letters opens with it, and what follows is the speaker's own description from the vision in chapter 1.

decisions.choice: the sword from his mouth (1:16)
decisions.reason: This is the sword that comes from his mouth in 1:16, and 2:16 says he will fight with it. It stands for the power of his word to judge.

decisions.choice: Pergamum: a royal city and a center of worship of the emperor
decisions.reason: Pergamum, north of Smyrna, had been a royal capital and was a seat of Roman government in the province. In 29 BC it built the first temple in Asia to Augustus and Rome. It also had a great altar to Zeus and a famous shrine of the healing god Asclepius.

decisions.choice: angel (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Revelation 1:20 says the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and every level keeps "angel" here as there. The note on 1:20 gives the other view.

records.literal_gloss: I know where you dwell, where the throne of the Satan [is], and you hold fast the name of me, and not you denied the faith of me even in the days of Antipas, the witness of me, the faithful [one] of me, who was killed among you, where the Satan dwells.

en.L: I know where you live, where the throne of Satan [is]; and you hold fast {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name, and you did not deny {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faith even in the days of Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful one, who was killed among you, where Satan lives.
en.B: I know where you make your home: the place of Satan's throne. Still you keep a firm grip on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name. Even in the days of Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} faithful one, who was killed among you where Satan lives, you did not disown your faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I know where you live. It is the city where Satan has his throne. But you hold on tightly to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You did not give up your faith in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, even when Antipas was killed in your city. He was {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} witness and was faithful to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Your city is where Satan lives.

fr.L: Je sais où tu habites : là où [est] le trône de Satan ; et tu tiens ferme {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom, et tu n’as pas renié {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} foi, même aux jours d’Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} témoin, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fidèle, qui a été tué chez vous, là où Satan habite.
fr.B: Je sais où tu habites : là où se trouve le trône de Satan. Pourtant, tu restes fermement attaché à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} nom. Même au temps d’Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} témoin et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fidèle, qui a été tué chez vous, là où Satan habite, tu n’as pas renié ta foi en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Je sais où tu vis. C’est la ville où Satan a son trône. Mais tu restes fermement attaché à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Tu n’as pas abandonné ta foi en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, même quand Antipas a été tué dans votre ville. C’était {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} témoin, et il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}est resté fidèle. Votre ville est l’endroit où Satan habite.

es.L: Sé dónde habitas, donde [está] el trono de Satanás; y retienes {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre, y no negaste {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} fe ni siquiera en los días de Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} testigo, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} fiel, que fue muerto entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, donde habita Satanás.
es.B: Sé dónde vives: allí donde está el trono de Satanás. Aun así, te aferras a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} nombre. Ni siquiera en los días de Antipas, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} testigo y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} fiel servidor, al que mataron entre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, allí donde vive Satanás, renegaste de tu fe en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Sé dónde vives. Es la ciudad donde Satanás tiene su trono. Pero tú te aferras a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. No abandonaste tu fe en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, ni siquiera cuando mataron a Antipas en tu ciudad. Él era {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} testigo y {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fue fiel. Tu ciudad es el lugar donde vive Satanás.

sw.L: Najua unakoishi, mahali kilipo kiti cha enzi cha Shetani; nawe unalishika jina {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} kwa nguvu, wala hukuikana imani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} hata katika siku za Antipa, shahidi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, mwaminifu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, aliyeuawa kwenu, mahali Shetani anapoishi.
